title: RWB-P7-E2004-APP: the wire shape of the rule-catalogue answer, the payload fields of the plan-timer decision record, the text of MSG-P7-009, the ledger writer identity and the physical registry columns are fixed by no source in the read set
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-11); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 14, 20, 27 and 28); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 15 and 16); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2.md (T3.1 defines decision_log_entry and approval only); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P7 Decision center and log v3.md (A2.1 to A2.5); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 004 Treatment entity and plan timers data model v2.md (sections 3, 11, 12 and 14); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case (Case and workflow)/RWB P3 E2004 CON Treatment entity and plan timers data model - contract v1.md (section 12.2 and 12.8)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 AC1, AC3 and AC4; 8 BR5; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.4; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: Five values this slice needs are given by no source in the read set, and each is written as a placeholder rather than a guess. (a) The wire shape of the rule-catalogue answer is not defined: the legacy story declares RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion) returning a RuleRow and RWB-P3-E2004-CON consumes GET /rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=, but neither names the media type, the element names, whether the package code and the version state travel with the row, or whether the outputs are a JSON object or an array. (b) The fields that carry the business date, the treatment identifier, the timer specification identifier and the target state inside rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 are not named by any source; the envelope fixes the record shape and the idempotency key only. (c) No text or field list is written for MSG-P7-009, which refuses a record with a missing rule version or an unknown decision code: the FSD P7 exception flows name the message and its two {field} values but not its wording. (d) The value of the actor of a system-written entry is given as an actor user identifier, while the writer is a service; no source states whether the service identity string or a system user row is written. (e) The physical types, lengths and nullability of rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case are given by no source: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 defines decision_log_entry and approval and stops there.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 27 gives the registry as package, version, workbook, generated DRL, SHA-256, valid-from date and approver with no wire shape; Temporal and Drools design slide 15 names the six version states and the fetch-verify-swap with no payload; RWB-P3-E2004-CON section 12.2 lists the catalogue operation as consumed and section 12.8 fakes it by rule ID and version only; the legacy story section 12 declares RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion) and the events table gives the record direction and three payload facts, and its section 14 gives MSG-P7-009 with no text; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 use MSG-P7-009 naming 'ruleVersion' and 'decisionCode' with no wording; DF-DEC-030 is actor_user_id and DF-DEC-004 and DF-DEC-005 are the rule identity, in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.
owner_role: Service owner of rwb-decision with the solution architect and the API owner
proposed: Publish in the rwb-decision contract the element names and media type of the catalogue answer (rule ID, rule version, package code, version state, Drools rule name, rule table, row order, action text, owner role, timer specification, target queue code, outputs), the fields that carry the business date, the treatment identifier, the timer specification identifier and the target state in the decision record, the text and field list of MSG-P7-009, the actor value of a system-written entry and the physical columns of the four registry tables; until then the story, its fakes and its tests carry the shapes of ASM-B2-P7-019-1 to ASM-B2-P7-019-4.

title: RWB-P7-E2004-APP: the rule-catalogue read that two stories consume is attributed to no owner in the Ownership Map, while the entry read the same map attributes to this service is served by RWB-P7-E2005-APP
source: _work/msr/context/P7.md (the 19 REST rows owned by P7); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-04, DP-11, DP-13); _work/msr/extract/B-TECH-04/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case (Case and workflow)/RWB P3 E2004 CON Treatment entity and plan timers data model - contract v1.md (section 12.2); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P7 rwb-decision (Decision and rules)/RWB P7 E2005 APP Decision log query API for audit v1.md (section 12.1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 004 Treatment entity and plan timers data model v2.md (section 12)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 AC1 and AC2; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.9; 18 Traceability
description: The catalogue read has no owning operation and the entry read has a second owner. (a) RWB-P3-E2004-CON consumes GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion= for the action text, owner role, timer specification and outputs of R-RES-25 and R-RES-27, and the legacy story declares the same read as the published interface RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion); the Ownership Map attributes no such operation to P7, whose 19 rows are the /admin/rule-package* family, /admin/rule-versions, /approvals*, /cases/{caseId}/recommendation and /decision-log. (b) The same map attributes GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} to P7, and RWB-P7-E2005-APP owns both as API-P7-006 and API-P7-007, so this slice cannot serve the approval-entry read the treatment side needs without double-claiming a path. (c) The result is that the one read this slice must provide is unowned and the two reads it must not provide are owned, so a consumer following the map and a consumer following the contract story would each hold a different surface. This story declares the catalogue read only, on the P7 base, and points the entry read at RWB-P7-E2005-APP.
evidence: P7 context pack ownership rows: GET /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/dry-run, GET /admin/rule-packages, GET /admin/rule-packages/change-report, GET /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions, GET /admin/rule-versions, GET /approvals, GET /approvals/{approvalId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/recommendation, GET /decision-log, GET /decision-log/{entryId} and the eight POST rows, with no rule-catalog row; RWB-P3-E2004-CON section 12.2 row 3 consumes GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion= from P7 and section 12.8 fakes it for R-RES-25 and R-RES-27 at RES-2026.12; RWB-P7-E2005-APP section 12.1 serves API-P7-006 GET /decision-log and API-P7-007 GET /decision-log/{entryId}; the legacy story section 12 publishes RuleCatalog.row(String ruleId, String packageVersion).
owner_role: Solution architect with the API owner and the rwb-decision service owner
proposed: Add GET /rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion= to the Ownership Map as a P7 row before the wave 2 contract baseline is tagged, and state in the same revision that the entry read is API-P7-007 of RWB-P7-E2005-APP so no second story claims it; if the catalogue read is instead to travel inside a model answer, restate RWB-P3-E2004-CON and this story on that path and retire the catalogue path from the consumed set.

section: Metadata (Depends on (build); Contract dependencies); 3 Preconditions; 6 INVEST check; 12.2; 13 Pattern application
description: The pattern list of this story carries twelve DP rows that add dependencies the metadata rows do not show. (a) DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-04 adds H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, DP-06 adds H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON, DP-07 adds H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-09 adds H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, DP-10 adds H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, DP-14 adds H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, DP-15 adds H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON, while the plan line gives Depends on (build) = None and one contract dependency. (b) DP-10 is the sharp case: its H row is the workflow kit, yet this slice registers no workflow and no Schedule, so the dependency the pattern adds is a kit this story uses only for the queue it listens on. (c) DP-06 adds a parameters dependency while this slice reads no parameter, because the cure period and the warning days stay with the owner of the plan step. (d) DP-04's C row RWB-P7-E1073-CON is a contract story of this service, so a reader cannot tell from the metadata whether it is consumed or published here.
evidence: WP B2-P7-019 story line: H [], C [RWB-P3-E2004-CON], patterns DP01, DP03, DP04, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP14, DP15, DP19. Context pack P7: schema rwb_decision, base /api/recovery/decision/v1, topic rwb.decision.events.v1, queue rwb-decision, wave 1 with a wave 2 business epic.
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform library owner and the rwb-decision service owner
proposed: State in R5.5 that a platform H row and a self-referential C row are held by the platform story and the contract story and are not repeated on a secondary APP line, or complete the metadata rows from the table; until then the story keeps the plan's rows, lists the patterns and reads their dependencies as added by the patterns rather than by the plan.

title: RWB-P7-E2004-APP: the legacy plan timers run on the Quartz timer check and publish a timer-due event, both retired in the target, and no source says what happens to a plan timer already running at cut-over
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-10, R5.7); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 42 and 44); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slide 4 and the change register T1 to T10); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 004 Treatment entity and plan timers data model v2.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 8, 12, 13 and 14)
section: 1 Story; 5 Exception paths; 8 BR10; 12.6 Schedules; 17 Guardrails; 18 Traceability
description: The legacy story states its plan timers as scheduled, paused, resumed and cancelled only through the TimerScheduler port, whose implementation in Epics 1 and 2 is JOB-05 Timer check, a five-minute Quartz job that expires a timer and publishes TimerDue (event 18); its acceptance criteria test that publication, that the timer status becomes EXPIRED and that JOB-05 is the only code that expires the timer. The target retires Quartz for Temporal Schedules and event-started workflows, and RWB-P3-E2004-CON states that TimerDue is retired and that the expiry is a fact of the workflow history; ADR-016 makes Schedules the replacement, but no source says what carries a plan timer that is already running when the monolith is cut over, whether the timer rows of the monolith are migrated into the workflow that owns the wait, or whether an operator re-establishes them. This story therefore states the ruling and builds nothing: it registers no Schedule, publishes no timer-due event and names no cut-over procedure.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-004 section 3 requires that every caller schedules through TimerScheduler, section 4 step 7 and section 12 name JOB-05 as the Quartz implementation that raises TimerDue, section 8 BR11 forbids any other write to the timer table and AC2, AC12 and AC14 assert the expiry and the event; Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44 list Temporal Schedules in the owning service and record Quartz as retired; RWB-P3-E2004-CON section 12.6 states that JOB-05 is retired with the TimerDue event and registers no Schedule; no read-set document gives a cut-over procedure for open timers.
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-case service owner and the platform workflow owner
proposed: Record in the Change Register how an INSTALLMENT_DUE or CURE_PERIOD timer that is running at cut-over is carried into the workflow that owns the wait, and remove the legacy steps 7 and 14 and AC2, AC12 and AC14 timer assertions from the target test set; until then the owning story states the durable timer and builds no Quartz path.
